title: Family
description: Introduce your family, ask about someone else's, and find your way through the Bengali words for relatives.

guide.title: The immediate family
guide.text:
মা (maa) mother; বাবা (baabaa) father; বাবা-মা or মা-বাবা parents.
ছেলে (chhele) son, boy; মেয়ে (meye) daughter, girl; ছেলেমেয়ে children.
স্বামী (shaamee) husband; স্ত্রী (stree) wife. The homely words are বর (bor) and বউ (bou).

Brothers and sisters are divided by age. ভাই and বোন are the general words for 'brother' and 'sister', but an elder brother or sister is always called দাদা or দিদি, so ভাই and বোন on their own are normally understood as younger ones.

দাদা (daadaa) elder brother - দিদি (didi) elder sister
ভাই (bhaai) younger brother - বোন (bon) younger sister
ভাইবোন (bhaaibon) brothers and sisters, siblings

Elder brothers and sisters are addressed as দাদা and দিদি, never by name alone; younger ones are called by name.

examples.english: We are three brothers and sisters.

guide.title: Father's side and mother's side
guide.text:
Uncles, aunts and grandparents have different names on the father's and the mother's side. These are the words used in West Bengal and by Bengali Hindus generally.

Father's side: ঠাকুরদা (thaakurdaa) grandfather; ঠাকুমা (thaakumaa) grandmother; জ্যাঠা (jyaathaa) father's elder brother; কাকা (kaakaa) father's younger brother; পিসি (pishi) father's sister.

Mother's side: দাদু (daadu) grandfather; দিদা (didaa) grandmother; মামা (maamaa) mother's brother; মাসি (maashi) mother's sister.

Many families use দাদু for both grandfathers.

Cousins are called brothers and sisters, with an adjective if you need to be exact: মামাতো ভাই (maamaato bhaai) 'son of my mother's brother', মাসতুতো বোন (maashtuto bon) 'daughter of my mother's sister'.

examples.english: My grandfather lives in the village.
He is my uncle (father's younger brother).

guide.title: The words used in Bangladesh
guide.text:
Bengali Muslims, and so most people in Bangladesh, use a partly different set, much of it from Persian and Arabic.

আব্বা (aabbaa) or আব্বু father; আম্মা (aammaa) or আম্মু mother
ভাইয়া (bhaaiyaa) or বড় ভাই elder brother; আপা (aapaa) or আপু elder sister
দাদা (daadaa) father's father; দাদি (daadi) father's mother
নানা (naanaa) mother's father; নানি (naani) mother's mother
চাচা (chaachaa) father's brother; ফুফু (phuphu) father's sister
মামা (maamaa) mother's brother; খালা (khaalaa) mother's sister

The trap is দাদা: in West Bengal it is an elder brother, in Bangladesh a paternal grandfather.

examples.english: She is my elder sister (Bangladesh usage).
My maternal grandfather lives in Dhaka.

guide.title: Respect inside the family
guide.text:
When you talk ABOUT an older relative, use the respectful verb ending -en: বাবা অফিসে আছেন; দাদু গ্রামে থাকেন. For a younger brother, a child or a friend, use the ordinary -e: আমার মেয়ে স্কুলে পড়ে।

When you talk TO them, most people today call their parents and elder brothers and sisters তুমি; আপনি to one's own parents is old-fashioned, though still heard. In-laws and other people's parents are আপনি.

To ask whether someone is married, Bengali says 'has your marriage happened?': আপনার কি বিয়ে হয়েছে? বিয়ে (biye) is 'wedding, marriage'.

Asking after the family is basic politeness: বাড়ির সবাই কেমন আছেন? - 'How is everyone at home?'

phrases.note: স before ত is a true s: stree.
The ব under স is silent.
'daadaa' is elder brother in West Bengal; a younger brother is 'bhaai' (ভাই). In Bangladesh দাদা is a paternal grandfather.

phrases.english: We are three brothers and sisters.

phrases.note: A question strangers ask quite freely.

phrases.english: How many people are there in your family?
My grandfather lives in the village.
phrases.note: 'daadu' is used for either grandfather; a paternal grandfather is also 'thaakurdaa' (ঠাকুরদা).
Specifically the son of a mother's brother.
